steps.message:
# Quarantine the lots under recall RC-2611

Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service, which you can use through the `inventory` MCP server.

A supplier has recalled lots of two of its parts under recall RC-2611. Its notice of 2026-09-10 and the amendment of 2026-09-12 are in `/app/recall/`, together with `part-map.csv`, which maps the supplier's part numbers to our item codes.

How stock is kept:

- Each lot is its own item. Its sku is the item code followed by the lot (for example `HP-4471-L26213-2` is lot 26213-2 of item code HP-4471), and its name gives the lot.
- Stock is held per storage location. The service calls locations warehouses: pass a location name wherever a tool takes `warehouse`. Locations are named `<site>-<bin>`, at three sites, `east`, `west` and `north`, and each site has a quarantine location `<site>-Q`.

What to do:

1. A lot is affected when the notice, as amended, covers it. Where the amendment and the notice differ, the amendment holds.
2. Quarantine every unit of an affected lot that is on hand outside a quarantine location: move it to the quarantine location of the same site. Record each move as two `adjust_stock` calls with reason `transfer` and reference `RC-2611`: the quantity taken out of the location it is in, and the same quantity added to `<site>-Q`.
3. A colleague started on 2026-09-11, working from the notice before the amendment came, and stopped partway. Their moves also use the reference `RC-2611`. Leave the moves that are right as they are. Where a move took units out of a location and never added them to the quarantine location, add them there. Where a move quarantined a lot that is not affected, move those units back to the location they came from, recorded the same way (out of `<site>-Q`, into that location).
4. Write `/app/RC-2611.csv`, a CSV file with the header `sku,quarantined,shipped` and one row per affected lot in the inventory, including lots with nothing left on hand. `quarantined` is the number of units of the lot in quarantine locations when you are done. `shipped` is the number of units of the lot shipped to customers: minus the sum of the lot's adjustments with reason `shipment`.

Do not change any other stock.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

arguments.command: cd /app/recall; ls -la; for f in *; do echo "=== $f"; cat "$f"; done

steps.reasoning_content:
Working out the day-of-year numbers, July 20 comes to day 201 and August 7 to day 219, so the lots 26201 through 26219 are the ones affected, leaving out line 3. I'm also checking whether any other items have lot names that need the same treatment.

Next I'm going through the lots one by one to see which fall in the affected date range, and marking the ones that match (e.g. 26201-2, 26207-1, 26210-2 for HX). For the HV lots I'm also checking the line-3 exception and the colleague's moves, and then doing the same pass on the HS batches, where batch 998 gets moved back to north-A01. Once that's settled I still need the per-warehouse stock and shipment figures for each affected lot.

Two items are being moved back: 26213-3 and 998. B993 has 30 pending to west-Q, and its north-A01 15 also goes to north-Q, out of the 45 it started with. East-DOCK is not a quarantine location, so that one just moves. The remaining moves are HX-26207-1 shifting east-B01 21 to east-Q and west-B01 16 to west-Q, and HX-26210-2 sending west-A01 23 to west.

I'm checking the remaining moves: north-B01 18 to north-Q, east-B02 12 to east-Q, and a handful of transfers from the east, west, and north buckets to their targets. Two reversals also need handling: 26213-3 and B998 get pulled back. Lots of calls here, so I'll batch them in parallel.

I confirmed that adj-267 is the id I had, and the earlier ids going up to 243 means other records exist as well, such as shipments. That's fine. Next I'm planning 13 moves, which works out to 26 calls, and I'll run them now.

I'm now pulling shipment records for the twelve affected lots, including 26201-2. For the adjustments, I'll query each SKU in pages of five, starting with page one for each, since the shipment adjustments are older and may need more pages.
I still need extra pages for several documents, so I'm listing which pages to fetch next, and I've ruled out the shell since only the provided tools are available.

I'm tallying the shipped counts per item: the shipment deltas are summed and negated, and most items come to a single total, with B1004 netting to 9 from its mixed signs.

I'm checking the quarantined lots against the affected window, with B1012 at 0 and the other counts listed alongside. Lot 26201 falls on July 20 and 26219 on August 7, so both are inside it, and B993's 15+30=45 checks out.

steps.message:
Quarantine for RC-2611 is done and both files are written. I didn't re-query the inventory after the moves. Each adjust call returned the expected on-hand figure, and the CSV and the quarantine totals come from my own tallies.

- **Affected lots:**
  - **Check valve KV-880:** production dates 2026-07-20 to 2026-08-07, excluding line 3. That is lot codes 26201 to 26219 under both item codes HX-2208 and HV-3310.
  - **Seal kit SK-412:** batches 985 to 1012, excluding 998.
  - **Total:** 13 lots, including HX-2208-L26201-2, which has nothing on hand.
- **Quarantine moves:** every unit of those lots outside a quarantine location went to the same site's `-Q`, recorded as a pair of transfers with reference `RC-2611`. That includes the 6 units of HV-3310-L26219-1 on the `east-DOCK` location.
- **Colleague's work:**
  - **Kept as is:** their moves for HV-3310-L26209-1, HV-3310-L26215-1 and HS-5120-B985 were right, so I left them.
  - **Unfinished move:** the HS-5120-B993 move had taken 30 units out of `west-B01` with no matching add, so I added them to `west-Q`.
  - **Reversed:** they had quarantined two unaffected lots. I returned HV-3310-L26213-3 (26 units, line 3) to `east-A02` and HS-5120-B998 (25 units, reworked) to `north-A01`.
- **Report:** `/app/RC-2611.csv` has one row per affected lot with quarantined and shipped counts. HS-5120-B1004's shipped figure is 9, because a +2 shipment correction offsets part of two earlier shipments. `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status "success".
